problem: There is a leftover drafting correction inside the text: 'Efficiency of any cycle is 1 − T_in,mean /... no: it is 1 − T_out,mean / T_in,mean'. A student reading this on a phone sees two contradictory formulas and a broken sentence.
fix: Write it once, cleanly: 'The efficiency of any reversible cycle is 1 − T_out,mean / T_in,mean, where T_in,mean is the mean temperature at which heat is supplied and T_out,mean is the mean temperature at which heat is rejected (Unit 3, Carnot's theorem).'

problem: The explanation says constant pressure addition 'puts the last part of the heat in while the gas is expanding and cooling'. During constant pressure heat addition the gas does expand, but its temperature keeps rising (dq = cp dT with dT > 0). There is no cooling, so the stated reason for the lower T_in,mean is wrong.
fix: Say: 'Constant volume addition raises the temperature fast — each kJ added raises T by 1/cv. Constant pressure addition raises it more slowly, by 1/cp per kJ, because part of the heat goes into expansion work. So for the same heat input at the same r the mean temperature of heat supply is lower, and less of the heat becomes work.' Also soften 'puts all the heat in at the highest temperature the cycle reaches' to 'puts the heat in at the top of compression, so the mean temperature of heat supply is highest'.

where: Section 2, paragraph 'MEP rises with r at fixed heat input'
problem: The wording 'the efficiency gain is larger than the loss of swept volume' is confusing: the swept volume does not fall, it grows with r, and that growth pushes MEP down rather than being a loss that has already happened. The quiz Q7 answer states the same idea correctly, so the two places disagree in wording.
fix: 'The swept volume per kg, v1(1 − 1/r), does grow with r at fixed v1, which by itself would lower MEP. But the efficiency rises faster in percentage terms, so the net work per kg grows faster than the swept volume and MEP rises.'
